correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and positive integral parking parameters, use the published exact facet and vertex descriptions to prove the exhaustive ridge incidence classes. The outward normal dot products give every angle. Count nested strict subset pairs by three-state assignments and account exactly for the missing (n-1)-subset and n special acute pairs when the first parameter is 1. Uniform ridge sampling differs exponentially little from an i.i.d. ternary partition, and the bivariate multinomial delta method has variance (3/4)^2*(2/3)=3/8, with unit derivative of the angle map. An independent vertex/facet/rank/normal enumerator passed 18 all-parameter instances n=3..5. This finite check is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Material primary full texts from 2022, 2024, and the 2025 online revision disclose the prerequisite facet and combinatorial face structure, but do not state a complete ambient Euclidean ridge dihedral-angle multiset or its sharp universal Gaussian sampling law. Checked published-finding corpus hits concern inballs, widths and vertex cone angles; none supports an equivalent angle-of-a-uniform-ridge result. Historical priority is not independently established, and immediate deducibility from strong prior ingredients is a specific residual risk.
residual_risks: The already published full face-lattice and facet normal formulas make the exact angle multiset directly derivable; an unlocated explicit published corollary might exist.
The source survey is focused on accessible core literature and semantic result records, not a complete systematic review of every stellohedron or generalized-permutahedron paper.
Some generic polytopal dihedral-angle enumeration framework could subsume the counting argument without using parking-function terminology.

value.rationale: A full Euclidean dihedral-angle multiset, rather than a selected facet count or a numerical sample, is a natural polytope geometry invariant. Uniform metric rigidity across all parking parameters, a sharp classical-only acute-ridge phenomenon, and the 135-degree Gaussian law with exact 3/8 fluctuation variance provide motivated structural and high-dimensional information not recoverable by merely knowing the number of ridges.
